title: Know your big clients: exposure, trust and health scores
course_title: Advanced Client Management: Keeping and Growing High-Value Clients

say: Know your big clients: exposure, trust and health scores.
This is the video for module one of Advanced Client Management.
A high-value account is a client who pays you regularly, often on a monthly retainer, and whose loss would hurt your income.
A retainer is a fixed fee for an agreed amount of ongoing work.

say: Managing these clients has three jobs. First, keep the account, by delivering reliably and communicating well.

say: Second, protect it, by spotting trouble before the client complains.

say: Third, grow it, through renewal at a fair price and extra work only where it truly helps the client.
But first, you need to know which clients matter most, in numbers, not feelings.

say: Here is a worked example. Ada runs a three-person digital marketing agency in Lagos. Her monthly team and office costs are about 900,000 naira.

card.title: How much does one client carry?
card.note: Example figures for practice, not market prices.

say: She lists each client's monthly fee. Client A pays 600,000 naira, Client B 250,000, Client C 200,000, and Clients D and E 150,000 and 100,000.

card.title: How much does one client carry?
card.note: Example figures for practice, not market prices.

say: Together that is 1,300,000 naira a month.
Client A's share is 600,000 divided by 1,300,000, which is about 46% of her income.
Without Client A, income falls to 700,000 naira, which is 200,000 below her costs every month.

say: That risk is called concentration risk: depending on one or two clients for a large share of your income. The cure is not to avoid big clients. It is to manage them with extra care.
Strategic clients get the owner or most senior person, a monthly check-in, and a quarterly review.

panel.heading: Match your time to the tier

cards.d: Large share of income, room to grow. Senior lead, monthly check-in, quarterly review.
Steady monthly fee, good fit. Named account lead, fortnightly update, review twice a year.
Small or occasional work, simple scope. Efficient service, templates, update at each delivery.

say: Key clients pay a steady monthly fee. They get a named account lead, an update every two weeks, and a review twice a year.

say: Standard clients get efficient service and an update at each delivery.
Tiers are about service level, not respect. Every client still deserves courtesy and on-time delivery. Review tiers every quarter.

say: Clients rarely leave because of one mistake. They leave when they stop trusting you. The Trust Equation breaks trust into four parts.
Credibility: you know your field and admit when you do not know.

panel.heading: The four parts of trust
items: Credibility: can I believe what you say?
Reliability: do you do what you said?
Intimacy: do I feel safe telling you things?

say: Reliability: reports arrive on the agreed day, and you call back when you said you would.

panel.heading: The four parts of trust

Intimacy: do I feel safe telling you things?

say: Intimacy: the client shares worries with you because you keep confidences and do not judge.

say: Self-orientation sits underneath the other three. When you push your own sales, it rises and trust falls.
For example, Ngozi, a bookkeeper, scored her reliability 4 after two late reports. She sent reports on the 5th of every month and stopped pitching, and her trust score rose from 3.4 to 7.0.

say: Lost accounts usually show warning signs weeks before the client says so. A health score collects those signs into one number.
Once a month, score five signals from 1, very poor, to 5, excellent.
The signals are your delivery, the client's responsiveness, their satisfaction, how they pay, and whether the sponsor, the decision-maker, stays engaged.
Give each a weight that adds to 100%, for example delivery 25%, responsiveness 15%, satisfaction 25%, payment 20% and sponsor 15%. Multiply each score by its weight and add.
Ada's Client A scored 3.25 out of 5. That is amber, even though it pays on time, because a new marketing director had never met her.
Use evidence: delivery dates, payment records and the client's own words. A score that drops from 4.4 to 3.6 over three months is more worrying than a steady 3.6.

panel.heading: Build an account health score
panel.rule: Score from facts, not your mood. Watch the trend.

say: Many accounts are lost because the one person who liked you leaves the company.

panel.heading: Do not rely on one contact

say: Build honest links with the person who approves payment, the person you work with daily, and someone senior who cares about results. Never go around your main contact to complain to their boss.

panel.heading: Do not rely on one contact

say: To remember. Know each client's share of your income. Match your time to the tier. Keep small promises and sell less. And score account health every month, acting quickly on amber or red.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Work out each client's share of your income
Sort clients into strategic, key and standard
Score account health monthly and act on amber
